headline: Margins expand despite top-line dip, guidance holds
summary_short: First Solar's Q2 FY2026 net sales fell 3.7% year-over-year to $1.06B on customer contract terminations, but diluted EPS rose 23% to $3.92 as gross margin widened to 57.3%. Adjusted EBITDA was $643.6M, and the company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 guidance unchanged.
summary_long: Net sales declined 3.7% y/y to $1.06B, driven by lower revenue from customer contract terminations, partially offset by higher third-party module volume. Despite the sales dip, gross profit rose 21.1% to $605.0M as cost of sales fell 24.5%, lifting gross margin to 57.3% from 45.6%. Operating income grew 24.5% to $450.4M and net income rose 23.6% to $422.6M ($3.92 diluted EPS), aided by higher interest income. Adjusted EBITDA was $643.6M, up 14.9% y/y. Cash and cash equivalents fell to $1.7B from $2.8B at year-end 2025 on seasonal working-capital needs and South Carolina facility capex. First Solar reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance unchanged across net sales, gross profit, capex, and Adjusted EBITDA, and issued Q3 Adjusted EBITDA guidance of $625-775M.

drivers.explanation: CEO Mark Widmar cited record H1 sales volume, surpassing 100GW of cumulative module sales globally, and a 45.1GW contracted backlog extending through 2030.
Decline was driven primarily by lower revenue from customer contract terminations, partially offset by an increase in the volume of modules sold to third parties.
Gross margin expanded to 57.3% from 45.6% as cost of sales fell 24.5% y/y even as net sales declined 3.7% — margin gain is fully explained by the cost line moving opposite to revenue.
Growth tracks the 24.5% operating income gain plus interest income more than doubling to $29.9M, partially offset by income tax expense rising to $36.8M from $10.3M.
